title: Split Fount
description: One big wood type word on cream stock, inked the way poster shops do a rainbow roll: three inks laid side by side in one fountain, blended by the roller into a gradient across the type. Drag across the sheet to run the press. The last proof is pulled away and the cylinder prints a fresh one under your hand, in the direction you dragged, and every pass the inks mix a little further on the roller, so the bands widen, drift and muddy from proof to proof. The ink is flat and a little uneven: squeezed dark at the letter edges, thin and speckled where the roller ran short, with the grain and nicks of the wood block and a faint bite of impression in the paper.
intent: After split-fount (rainbow roll) letterpress inking, as printed on wood type by poster shops such as Hatch Show Print and the Hamilton Wood Type museum: the gradient is the press, not decoration, and it changes with every proof. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split-fount_inking
